beside.why: Written by the services under the path you chose, and yours. lemonfiber never reads what is in them and never removes them.
The container engine's. lemonfiber starts and stops them and owns none of them; docker is what lists and removes them.
Docker, a media server running natively, a tunnel client. lemonfiber did not put them there and does not take them away.

kept.what: the settings file
kept.why: Every answer setup collected, and everything the stack is run with. It is handed to Compose as it stands, and it is the one file to keep if you keep one.

kept.what: the settings you recorded for plugins
kept.why: Each value you chose for a setting a plugin's service reads, by its name. A setting you never recorded is not here, and its service is written with the plugin's default.

kept.what: the secrets lemonfiber holds
kept.why: Every credential lemonfiber holds, its own included: each value a plugin's recipe captured, lemonfiber minted or you entered, by its name, with the one earlier value of each that undoing a change puts back, and the key the change journal's fingerprints of them are taken under. It is never written into the stack, and nothing records it anywhere else.

kept.what: each service's own secrets file
kept.why: One file per service that names a secret, written from the secrets above and handed to Compose for that service alone. Any run that writes the service's entry writes its file again.

kept.what: setup's saved progress
kept.why: What you had answered when you last stopped part-way through setup, so leaving resumes rather than restarts. It carries the credentials you had entered by then, and it is deleted the moment setup finishes.

kept.what: the web interface's password
kept.why: What proves the password you set for the web interface, kept as an Argon2id verifier and never as the password itself — there is no key that would turn it back. It is what lets the surface be offered to your network at all, and removing it takes that offer away.

kept.what: what pairing a phone rests on
kept.why: The certificate the web interface presents when it is served encrypted, and its key; this stack's own identifier, which a paired phone knows it by; and the port it was last served on. Removing it means every paired phone refuses this machine until it is paired again.

kept.what: the record of what left this machine
kept.why: When each outbound request went, what kind it was, and where it went — so what the enumeration says would be sent can be checked against what was. It carries no header, no body and no query, which is the whole of why it is safe to keep.

kept.what: what the release list last said
kept.why: When lemonfiber last asked which version of itself is newest, what the answer was, and how many of those asks went unanswered — which is what keeps a machine with no route out from reaching for the network on every run. Nothing about you and nothing about this machine ever goes the other way.

kept.what: what the line was declared to carry
kept.why: The share of the connection the stack was told to keep to, the hours it keeps them, and what the line has been seen to carry. Nothing about what was moved over it — only how much, and when.

kept.what: the change journal
kept.why: What the last run wrote, so a repair can be put back. The fields that changed and what they were — nothing about you and nothing about what you watch. A change to a credential is recorded by the fingerprints of its values, never by a value.

kept.what: the change journal's key
kept.why: What a change journal an earlier release wrote sealed its credentials with. It is read only to open them, so they are recorded by their fingerprints, and it is taken away the next time the journal is written.

kept.what: the expected-state baseline
kept.why: What lemonfiber last wrote into each service, which is the only way a later run can tell a value you changed from one it set itself and would otherwise write over.

kept.what: the record of what was written to the stack directory
kept.why: A checksum for each compose file lemonfiber wrote, so a file you edited by hand is recognised as yours rather than replaced on the next run.

kept.what: the quality choice
kept.why: Which preset is in force, for everything and per media type, so a later run applies the choice you made rather than the default.

kept.what: the notification choice
kept.why: How much you asked to be told about, and the individual events you set apart from that answer.

kept.what: your answer about starting on boot
kept.why: Whether you asked for the stack to come back after this machine restarts, which form that means, and whether the last thing you asked for was a stop. It is the answer you gave and not a claim that it works — on a Mac or a Windows machine, half of what makes it work is a Docker Desktop setting lemonfiber cannot write.

kept.what: which restart of this machine was last acted on
kept.why: So a run can tell a machine that has just restarted from one that has not, and report a boot that failed once rather than every time you type something. It is what this machine did, kept apart from what you asked for.

kept.what: what each service run on a schedule last did
kept.why: When each run-and-exit service last ran, how it ended and the lines a failed run wrote, its credentials withheld, so a missed time is made up once and a failed run is reported until one ends well.

kept.what: the monitors lemonfiber made in the outside watcher
kept.why: The id the watcher answered for each monitor lemonfiber provisioned, what each was asked to watch and what it watches instead where it could not. It is the only way a monitor is paired with the service, entry point or job it covers: never by its name or its address, which you may change in the watcher itself.

kept.what: the questions you have already settled
kept.why: The choices whose cost was stated to you once — running with no VPN, or with a provider that forwards no port — so they are not put to you again every run.

kept.what: why you turned a request down
kept.why: The request service has nowhere to keep a reason, so a refusal it sends carries none. This is lemonfiber's own note of what you said, so the person who asked can still be told why.

kept.what: what each person asked for of music and books
kept.why: No request service holds an ask for music or books, so lemonfiber keeps each one itself: what was asked, by whom, and whether you let it through or turned it down.

kept.what: which member each request asked as the request service's owner was for
kept.why: Where members ask as the request service's owner, the request service records each of those requests as the owner's, so lemonfiber keeps whose each one is: it counts toward that member's allowance and is listed as theirs.

kept.what: where music and book covers were fetched from
kept.why: A cover is fetched from wherever the curator says it is, so lemonfiber notes each host it fetched one from, and the account of what leaves this machine names them.

kept.what: where alerts are delivered
kept.why: Each notification back-end you added, who chose it, how far it is proven and what became of its deliveries, so a message that never arrived is told apart from one that was never sent.

kept.what: what each notification back-end is reached with
kept.why: The token each back-end takes messages with, kept apart from the list of back-ends so nothing that shows you where alerts go ever reads one.

kept.what: what each service tells the core what happened with
kept.why: The digest of the key each curator and the media server send what happened with, so an event is taken only from the service the key was handed to and the key itself is kept nowhere but there.

kept.what: when each person was handed a code
kept.why: The media server says which devices are signed in and nothing about a code handed over and not yet used. This is what tells somebody still to sign in from somebody never handed anything.

kept.what: where the request gate's record was last read
kept.why: The doctor reports what the request gate refused and removed since it last looked. This is the place it reached, so each refusal and removal is reported once.

kept.what: what is installed of somebody else's
kept.why: Each plugin you installed, and what installing it settled: the images it runs, the digest that fixes each one, the tier each is published on and where inside its container it keeps its own state. It is the only record that a stranger's service is on this machine, so losing it does not leave you with no plugins — it leaves you with plugins nothing can account for.

kept.what: what a plugin answered outside its contract
kept.why: Each answer an installed plugin's adapter gave that its contract does not allow. The plugin fills none of that capability until a proof it passes clears it, so losing this would let it fill one again unproven.

kept.what: what each installed plugin is run with again
kept.why: Each installed plugin's manifest and the starting files its run proofs use, kept once the install holds so the doctor and its demand recipes work after its source is gone. Removing a plugin takes its directory away.

kept.what: what each plugin's run proofs last came to
kept.why: Each run proof's last verdict, against the image, the arguments and the starting files it ran with, so the doctor runs it again only when one of those moves rather than on every diagnosis.

kept.what: the newest plugin catalogue this machine verified
kept.why: Which release of the signed plugin catalogue was the newest one checked here. An older release is still validly signed, and this is what refuses one that was replaced.

kept.what: the keys other programs reach the web interface with
kept.why: Each key's name, scope and the SHA-256 digest of its secret, never the secret itself. Removing an entry revokes that key, and removing the file revokes every one.

kept.what: when each key was last used
kept.why: When each key last reached the web interface, kept apart from the keys so writing it never rewrites them. It holds no part of any secret.

kept.what: the phones that may prove they are you
kept.why: The public half of each key a phone registered to stand in for your password when a key is minted, with what attested where it lives. Nothing here could sign anything.

kept.what: the phones that asked to be woken
kept.why: The address each phone's distributor gave, the keys a message is encrypted to, and how many it is owed. Without it no phone hears of an alert until it is opened.

kept.what: when each invitation was offered
kept.why: When each account nobody has claimed yet was offered. The media server's own record of when an account was made can lose it, and an invitation nobody can date is withdrawn.

kept.what: how long a request may wait for a decision
kept.why: What the household agreed about requests nobody rules on: how long one waits before it is closed. Without it nothing is closed, because nobody agreed to it.

kept.what: whose asking was taken away while the disk was full
kept.why: Each member whose permission to ask was taken away while the disk had no room, and what came off them, so exactly that is given back once there is room again.

kept.what: the port the egress guard last forwarded
kept.why: The port the VPN's egress guard last forwarded, which every torrent client was set to take, so a client is set again only when the guard's answer changes.

kept.what: how the queue has been healed
kept.why: Each unhealthy download's strikes, so one is acted on only after enough looks in a row find it wedged for the same reason; what the latest look found; and the newest runs, each with what was dropped, blocklisted and searched for again, and why.

kept.what: what you have been told, and what is still owed you
kept.why: Every alert decided and not yet delivered, and what was already said, so an alert held while a channel was down is delivered once it is back rather than lost.

kept.what: what is wrong, and since when
kept.why: Each condition the doctor found, since when it has held and whether you were told, so how long something has been broken and whether it comes and goes are answered across runs.

kept.what: which containers lemonfiber stopped itself
kept.why: Each container lemonfiber stopped, so one that exits with an error when told to stop reads as stopped rather than as a fault. Starting it again lets go of it.

kept.what: every repair lemonfiber carried out
kept.why: Each repair and what it came to, the ones that changed nothing included, so a repair that keeps failing to hold a fault down can be seen for what it is.

kept.what: how long each member's devices may play
kept.why: The last day each member's client spoke to the media server. A grant lasts a set number of days from then, and the devices on one that ran out are signed out.

kept.what: the live streams opened for members
kept.why: Each live stream the media server opened for a member, with whom it was opened for, the channel and what closes it, so one whose pass lapsed unrenewed, or a removed member's, is closed. No pass is kept, and a stream is forgotten once it is closed.

kept.what: the words you have gone and looked up
kept.why: So a report names a word you already know instead of explaining it again. What one person has been told is not what another has, which is why this is kept here rather than beside the stack.

kept.what: the materialised stack
kept.why: The project Compose is pointed at and every service's starting files, written out of the stack description this build carries. Any run that starts something writes them again.

kept.what: each service's own configuration
kept.why: The directories the containers mount and write their own settings, databases and API keys into. What is in them is theirs rather than lemonfiber's, and this is the largest thing here by far.

kept.what: the backup archives
kept.why: Each one a copy of the configuration above, so an archive holds whatever that held — the credentials included. Nothing sends one anywhere.

kept.what: the support bundles kept for a browser
kept.why: A bundle asked for from the web surface is written here so it can be handed back to the browser that asked for it. Every value in one is replaced by a stand-in before it is written, and nothing sends one anywhere either.

kept.what: what a command this machine keeps running has said
kept.why: A command handed to this machine's service manager has no terminal to speak in, so what it would have said goes here instead — one file per command, appended to. It is the only record of what a guard or a clock did while nobody was watching. Removing it loses that history and stops nothing.

kept.what: what the disk could do last time
kept.why: Whether importing by hardlink worked when it was last looked at, so losing that capability is noticed rather than showing up as a disk filling twice as fast. Losing this costs one run's history and nothing else.

roots.what: Your answers, and lemonfiber's memory of what it wrote. Small, worth keeping a copy of, and the half that cannot be made again.
What can be made again: the materialised stack, each service's own configuration, the archives, the bundles, and what a command this machine keeps running has said.
